# /crav1-add-to-spec

[All skills](../skills.md) · Walkthrough: [From new information to an existing spec](../../from-add.md) · Playbook: [`SKILL.md`](../../../.cursor/skills/crav1/crav1-add-to-spec/SKILL.md)

## Purpose

Bring new information into existing specs; asks what you have: a fact, a dump, a code change, or a meeting.

**[`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md)** opens with one question: what you have, a fact, a dump, a code change, or a meeting (minutes, a transcript, a mail, or a chat). It skips the question when the message shows which. It replaces match-dump-to-specs, code-into-specs, and meeting-to-specs; their rules are kept as branches, and a kept quote from any of them goes through the fact rules.

A fact (was [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md)): New information aimed at one spec that already exists is **[`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md)**. [`/crav1-tighten-spec`](crav1-tighten-spec.md) stays for mushy wording. Match, intake, spark, and ideas create the folders. This command does not plan.

A fact (was [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md)): New information for one existing spec → quote it into that `spec.md`, then report whether the landscape or another spec has to change. Does not rewrite those other files unless asked. Does not create a glossary. A new glossary row can be one listed edit and is not written unless apply is chosen. A meaning the new information does not state is `to be researched`. Existing rows are not rewritten. Does not plan, implement, or commit.

A dump (was `/crav1-match-dump-to-specs`): A later dump, specs already exist → sort onto those specs (belongs, already there, or does not fit), then quote the new bits. The whole dump is written as one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` (1.61.0). Does not ask for a slug first. Does not create a slug. Does not seed `docs/system/`. Fills a missing `glossary.md` only when that folder already exists. New glossary rows are appended. Existing rows are not rewritten. A meaning the source does not state is `to be researched`. That same pass adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. It does not rewrite what is already there. Does not plan, implement, or commit.

A code change (was `/crav1-code-into-specs`): A code change that already landed, specs already exist → sort onto those specs (belongs, already described there, or fits none), then quote what the change does. No dump. Does not ask for a slug first. Does not create a slug. Does not watch the repo. Does not seed `docs/system/`. Fills a missing `glossary.md` only when that folder already exists. New glossary rows are appended. Existing rows are not rewritten. A meaning the source does not state is `to be researched`. That same pass adds what is new to the short description, the diagram, and how the parts connect. It does not rewrite what is already there. Does not plan, implement, or commit.

A meeting (was `/crav1-meeting-to-specs`): When the user brings minutes, a transcript, an email, or a chat thread, **[`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md)** extracts the requirements, decisions, changes, open questions, and bugs, and matches each quote to specs that already exist. An email or a chat thread is accepted as well as minutes or a transcript. The kind is `meeting`, `email`, or `chat`, from what the input shows. The date comes from the input. Each item is a quote, with speaker and time when the input shows them. Small talk is dropped. When more than one existing spec could fit, every candidate stays listed. Nothing is dropped to keep the list short. Each item that matches an existing spec shows one line, `State: <state>.`, and a short reason that names the evidence, in the item block and in the question. The states are built, partly built, planned, and not built. `Fits: none` has no state line. Evidence is that slice’s `spec.md` (including `## Match`), `plan.md`, `tasks.md` checkboxes, and `verify.md` when present. When those do not settle it, one read-only look at the code that spec or plan points to. A code-based or uncertain state is labeled `(inference, not in the docs)`. The line does not change keep, leave, or dismiss. It is not written and it is not passed to [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) as quote text. The user takes them one at a time: keep, leave, or dismiss. The whole input is always written once as one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` by source date (1.61.0); a left item stays in that note. Dismiss is for this run only. The next run starts fresh. A kept addition goes to that spec through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). The quote starts with `From <kind> <date>.` when there is a date, otherwise `From <kind>.` The impact check still runs there. A kept new feature names [`/crav1-spark-to-spec`](crav1-spark-to-spec.md), [`/crav1-ideas-to-spec`](crav1-ideas-to-spec.md), or [`/crav1-bundle-to-specs`](crav1-bundle-to-specs.md). A kept bug names [`/crav1-fix-bug`](crav1-fix-bug.md). Those commands are not run. When a kept addition imports a source, the skill writes `docs/sources/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/` following the imported-sources convention and does not write the spec. It does not commit. It is cross-cutting. It may run from any lane. It does not move work into a lane. It is a later skill. It is not a starter option. Asking for startup options names only the six and does not run this command. The six starter options stay unchanged.

A meeting (was `/crav1-meeting-to-specs`): Minutes, a transcript, an email, or a chat thread → quotes matched to existing specs, keep, leave, or dismiss one at a time; the whole input is one full note. A kept addition goes through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md). A clear answer to a spec open question is linked under it.

1.64.0: a code change can name a repo and branch (`code change orders-api feat/orders-retry`); the code is read read-only from `../<repo>`. The branch diff starts at the fork point (the repo's `Merges into` branch, the default branch, or another spec branch), the slice `Synced at` line keeps one entry per branch, a yes records `Merges into` in `repos.md`, and the note's `commits:` list plus `git patch-id` stop a commit being imported twice, also after a rebase.

1.65.0: a code change can be a pull request (`code change orders-api PR 71`, or its URL). It writes or reuses the PR note (the pull request's title and description, `kind: pull request`) and links it from the code-change note with `pr_note:`. Given a branch, it writes the PR note when a signed-in `gh` or `az` host shows exactly one pull request for that branch; otherwise it says why it wrote none.

## Choice words

Exact words for bots and scripted runs (no `--flags`). A word in the invocation takes that choice without asking. A headless or bot run with no word stops and names the valid words.

| Question | Word | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What you have | `fact` | one fact |
| What you have | `dump` | a dump |
| What you have | `code change` | a code change |
| What you have | `meeting` | a meeting (minutes, transcript, mail, or chat) |

## Runs when

New information for specs that already exist. Called by the user, by [`/crav1-read-environment`](crav1-read-environment.md) for a confirmed Match section, by [`/crav1-suggest-tests-for-code`](crav1-suggest-tests-for-code.md) for one kept or dismissed suggestion, by [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) for one kept addition, by [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md) for a preview change, and by [`/crav1-ado-sync`](crav1-ado-sync.md) for one kept change or one answer.

## Reads

In short: A fact: That information and one `spec.md`; A dump: The dump and existing spec folders; A code change: A commit, range, or branch diff, plus specs; A meeting: That input and existing spec folders.

A fact: Reads the new information and one existing `spec.md`. A dump: Reads the dump, existing spec folders, skipping `_template`, and the generated notes indexes so the same source is not imported twice. A code change: Reads a named commit, range, or branch diff, and existing spec folders. A meeting: Reads the minutes, transcript, email, or chat after the command, and existing `docs/specs/<slug>/` folders, skipping `_template`. For an item that matches a slice, also reads that slice’s `spec.md` (including `## Match`), `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and `verify.md` when present, and the code that spec or plan points to only when those files do not settle the build state.

## Writes

In short: Every kind: one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` by source date and the generated indexes; A fact: Short quotes in that spec with a `Full source:` link, `docs/sources/` for an imported source, the transfer data policy after a yes, research stale marks after a yes, and answer links under open questions; A dump: Confirmed new quotes in matching specs, `docs/sources/` for an imported source, the transfer data policy after a yes, research stale marks after a yes, and answer links under open questions; A code change: Quotes of what belongs in matching specs, a missing `glossary.md` or new glossary rows when `docs/system/` exists, the picture update, `Synced at` (repo cell or slice line), and research stale marks after a yes; other listed edits only on apply; A meeting: A source folder when a kept addition imports one, the transfer data policy after a yes; answer links and asked marks through [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md).

Auto-accept applies to those recommendations only when the transfer data policy clearly covers them. A meeting handoff that already wrote the folder only adds those lines. ## Does not

A fact: Leaves `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and a missing `glossary.md` alone. Does not commit. A dump: Leaves leftovers, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and other landscape files alone unless the user picks apply. Does not commit. A code change: Leaves leftovers, application code, `plan.md`, `tasks.md`, and other landscape files alone unless the user picks apply. Does not commit. A meeting: Leaves `docs/system/`, specs, marks, and dismissals alone. Does not commit.

Limits and exceptions: A fact: creates no slug and no `docs/system/`. Every input is one full note in `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/` (source date, `Imported:` date); never absorbed, `used_by` grows; no Note choice; indexes generated. The research question is not the landscape apply question. The read-environment and suggest-tests-for-code handoffs ask once at the end of the run, not per item, whether to run [`/crav1-refresh-system-notes`](crav1-refresh-system-notes.md), and do not run it. The ado-sync handoffs do not ask. The meeting handoff runs this research check. It does not run it a second time. A dump: creates no slug and seeds no `docs/system/`. The whole dump is one full note. The research question is not the landscape apply question. A code change: creates no slug, seeds no `docs/system/`, and does not watch the repo. The research question is not the landscape apply question. A skill that writes `docs/research/` follows the clear section of that same file. That check does not ask the user. A meeting: no input stops and asks. The kind and the date come from the input, one of each for the run. An unclear kind, or no date, is one question. The whole input is one full note; there is no Note choice. Dismiss is this run only and is not stored. Dismiss stays for a greeting, scheduling, and thanks. A kept new feature or bug only names the next command. A build-state line on a matched item is informational. It is not quote text. It does not start Specify, Plan, or Build. It is not a starter option.

## You run next / Runs by itself

- You run next: [`/crav1-tighten-spec`](crav1-tighten-spec.md); [`/crav1-finalize-commit`](crav1-finalize-commit.md)
- Runs by itself: A fact: Calls no skill. A dump: Calls no skill. A code change: Calls no skill. A meeting: Calls [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) for one kept addition. That handoff runs the research check in `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/research-stale.md`. This skill does not run it a second time and does not write the stale block. A clear answer to a spec open question is handed to [`/crav1-add-to-spec`](crav1-add-to-spec.md) as an answer link without a keep question, with the asked marks the input shows, following `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/open-questions.md`. An unclear or partial answer is shown as a possible answer and the question stays open.

<the new information, in your words>
